scene-u01.name: KP09 L1 regularization and the soft threshold

frame-u01.name: KP09 L1 regularization and the soft threshold
frame-u01.text: KP09 L1 regularization and the soft threshold

scene-u01-pnew1-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew1-25.text: The ideal sparsity penalty is $\ell_0$, but it has two problems

scene-u01-pnew1-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew1-26.text: $\ell_0$: counts how many coordinates are non-zero (KP07).

scene-u01-pnew1-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew1-28.text: problem 1: doubling leaves the count unchanged

scene-u01-pnew1-140.name: text#140
scene-u01-pnew1-140.text: Doubling $\mathbf x$ leaves $\ell_0$ unchanged: the homogeneity a norm requires fails.

scene-u01-pnew1-142.name: text#142
scene-u01-pnew1-142.text: per the source: minimizing it is NP-hard.

scene-u01-pnew1-144.name: text#144
scene-u01-pnew1-144.text: NP-hard: with many features one tries every combination ($16$ already for $n=4$).

scene-u01-pnew1-146.name: text#146
scene-u01-pnew1-146.text: $\ell_0$ is the most direct yet too hard to compute; we need its nearest tractable stand-in.

scene-u01-pnew2-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew2-25.text: The fix: replace it with the nearest convex function, the $\ell_1$ norm (lasso)

scene-u01-pnew2-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew2-43.text: lasso = least absolute shrinkage and selection operator

scene-u01-pnew2-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew2-45.text: $\ell_1$ is convex, so when $J$ is convex the whole objective is convex and reliable algorithms exist.

scene-u01-pnew2-47.name: text#47
scene-u01-pnew2-47.text: Analogy: $\ell_0$ is a flat monthly fee for using it at all; $\ell_1$ charges by amount used.

scene-u01-pnew2-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew2-49.text: Swap the hard $\ell_0$ for the tractable $\ell_1$: lasso.

scene-u01-pnew3-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew3-25.text: The price: $|x|$ has a corner at $0$, the source of exact zeros

scene-u01-pnew3-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew3-38.text: The corner "sucks" the solution onto $0$: computed next.

scene-u01-pnew3-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew3-40.text: Price: not differentiable, handled with the "subgradient".

scene-u01-pnew3-62.name: text#62
scene-u01-pnew3-62.text: $\ell_1$ is tractable (convex) and has a corner (can reach zero).

scene-u01-pnew4-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew4-25.text: First the simplest case: one coordinate

scene-u01-pnew4-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew4-26.text: $J$'s quadratic approximation is $\tfrac12 h(x-x^{\ast})^2$, $h>0$, plus the $\ell_1$ penalty.

scene-u01-pnew4-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew4-39.text:
blue: $\tfrac12h(x-x^{\ast})^2$ (fit the data)
green: $\alpha|x|$ (stay simple, with a corner)

scene-u01-pnew4-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew4-41.text: The minimum must satisfy "$0$ belongs to the subgradient".

scene-u01-pnew4-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew4-43.text: Next, three cases locate the minimum.

scene-u01-pnew5-67.name: text#67
scene-u01-pnew5-67.text: In case 3, $-hx^{\ast}+\alpha s=0$ has a solution only if $|hx^{\ast}|\le\alpha$ (the corner pulls the minimum onto $0$).

scene-u01-pnew5-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew5-69.text: The threshold is $\alpha/h$: beyond it shift, within it zero.

scene-u01-pnew6-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew6-25.text: The three cases together: the soft threshold

scene-u01-pnew6-96.name: text#96
scene-u01-pnew6-96.text: Coefficients within the threshold are switched off to $0$; those beyond it shift toward zero by $\alpha/h$, direction unchanged. Like an eraser removing faint strokes and shortening the rest.

scene-u01-pnew6-98.name: text#98
scene-u01-pnew6-98.text: Soft threshold: small ones to zero, big ones shifted.

scene-u01-pnew7-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew7-26.text: Three $x^{\ast}$: above the threshold, within it, and negative; orange = $\ell_1$ soft threshold, blue = $\ell_2$.

scene-u01-pnew7-89.name: text#89
scene-u01-pnew7-89.text: All three were checked by minimizing $\tfrac12h(x-x^{\ast})^2+\alpha|x|$ directly on a fine grid: grid minima $0.7000$, $0.0000$, $-0.3000$.

scene-u01-pnew7-91.name: text#91
scene-u01-pnew7-91.text: $\ell_1$ sends $0.3$ to zero; $\ell_2$ only shrinks it to $0.2$.

scene-u01-pnew8-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew8-25.text: In the picture: $\ell_1$ has a "dead zone", $\ell_2$ does not

scene-u01-pnew8-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew8-46.text: Between the gold dashed lines the output is $0$ whatever $x^{\ast}$ is.

scene-u01-pnew8-48.name: text#48
scene-u01-pnew8-48.text: Outside it: parallel to the diagonal, a fixed $0.5$ lower; $\ell_2$ shrinks large coefficients proportionally more.

scene-u01-pnew8-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew8-50.text: The green dots are the last page's $1.2\to0.7$, $0.3\to0$, $-0.8\to-0.3$.

scene-u01-pnew9-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew9-25.text: Many coordinates: swap "add a penalty" for "draw a constraint region"

scene-u01-pnew9-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew9-26.text: The equivalent constrained form (duality): minimize $J$ within $\|\mathbf x\|_1\le r$; the larger $\alpha$, the smaller the equivalent $r$.

scene-u01-pnew9-38.name: text#38
scene-u01-pnew9-38.text: $J$'s contours are ellipses; the minimum is where an ellipse growing from $\mathbf x^{\ast}$ first touches the region.

scene-u01-pnew9-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew9-40.text: Added: with two coordinates $\ell_1$ is a diamond, $\ell_2$ a circle.

scene-u01-pnew9-42.name: text#42
scene-u01-pnew9-42.text: The diamond has corners, the circle is smooth: the difference is where the ellipse touches.

scene-u01-pnew10-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew10-25.text: Same contours: the circle is touched mid-arc, the diamond at a corner

scene-u01-pnew10-56.name: text#56
scene-u01-pnew10-56.text: The corner pulls the solution onto an axis: the geometric intuition for exact zeros in $\ell_1$.

scene-u01-pnew11-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew11-26.text: Same $\mathbf x^{\ast}$, only $\mathbf H$ replaced by another positive-definite matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1.5&-0.9\\-0.9&1\end{pmatrix}$.

scene-u01-pnew11-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew11-28.text: another $\mathbf H$: ellipse shape and direction change

scene-u01-pnew11-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew11-43.text: The minimum on the diamond becomes $(0.9372,\,0.0628)$: not on an axis.

scene-u01-pnew11-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew11-45.text: $\mathbf H$'s eigenvalues change from about $0.52,\,2.98$ to $0.32,\,2.18$.

scene-u01-pnew11-72.name: text#72
scene-u01-pnew11-72.text: The corner makes exact zeros "easy", not certain.

scene-u01-pnew12-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew12-25.text: The statistics: $\ell_1$ often lands on an axis, $\ell_2$ almost never

scene-u01-pnew12-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew12-26.text: $2819$ random $\mathbf x^{\ast}$ and positive-definite $\mathbf H$ (fixed seed, with $\|\mathbf x^{\ast}\|_1>1$); each square $=1\%$.

scene-u01-pnew12-246.name: text#246
scene-u01-pnew12-246.text: the corner easily hits an axis

scene-u01-pnew12-247.name: text#247
scene-u01-pnew12-247.text: the circle rarely hits an axis

scene-u01-pnew12-249.name: text#249
scene-u01-pnew12-249.text: The $0.1\%$ is a grid-resolution boundary artefact; in theory the probability is $0$. Numbers from the lecture (not re-run).

scene-u01-pnew12-251.name: text#251
scene-u01-pnew12-251.text: The $\ell_1$ corner makes exact zeros common; $\ell_2$ almost never.

scene-u01-pnew13-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew13-25.text: The soft-threshold formula assumes independent coordinates ($\mathbf H$ diagonal)

scene-u01-pnew13-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew13-26.text: A general $\mathbf H$ is not diagonal: thresholding coordinate by coordinate is not the right answer.

scene-u01-pnew13-64.name: text#64
scene-u01-pnew13-64.text: Coordinate-wise soft threshold (thresholds $\alpha/h_{jj}=0.5,\ 0.667$): objective $2.3167$; the true lasso solution $2.1474$ (lower).

scene-u01-pnew13-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew13-66.text: Added: in practice one repeats coordinate updates until stable (coordinate descent).

scene-u01-pnew13-68.name: text#68
scene-u01-pnew13-68.text: The soft-threshold formula holds only in the diagonal case; the general case needs an iterative algorithm.

scene-u01-pnew14-25.name: text#25
scene-u01-pnew14-25.text: A practical reminder, and the next question

scene-u01-pnew14-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew14-26.text: The larger $\alpha$, the more zeros; but larger is not always better.

scene-u01-pnew14-32.name: text#32
scene-u01-pnew14-32.text: few zeros → too few features dropped

scene-u01-pnew14-34.name: text#34
scene-u01-pnew14-34.text: too large → useful features also switched off

scene-u01-pnew14-36.name: text#36
scene-u01-pnew14-36.text: Choose $\alpha$ as KP07 said, by a validation set or cross-validation.

scene-u01-pnew14-70.name: text#70
scene-u01-pnew14-70.text:
both $\ell_2$ and $\ell_1$ change the objective;
can we change nothing and just train fewer steps?

scene-u01-pnew14-74.name: text#74
scene-u01-pnew14-74.text: Next: without touching the objective, can training fewer steps do the same? KP10.

steps.label: KP09 L1 regularization and the soft threshold
KP09 · 1/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Left: for x = (0, 3, 0, 0, −2, 1) the non-zero count stays 3 after doubling; right: the 16 cards are all "which coordinates are non-zero" combinations for n = 4.) KP08's ℓ2 only shrinks and never zeroes, so it cannot pick a few useful features. The ideal sparsity penalty is KP07's ℓ0: count the non-zero coordinates.

steps.label: KP09 · 1/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Left: for x = (0, 3, 0, 0, −2, 1) the non-zero count stays 3 after doubling; right: the 16 cards are all "which coordinates are non-zero" combinations for n = 4.) KP08's ℓ2 only shrinks and never zeroes, so it cannot pick a few useful features. The ideal sparsity penalty is KP07's ℓ0: count the non-zero coordinates.

steps.label: KP09 · 1/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Problem 1: not a true norm, ‖2x‖₀ = ‖x‖₀, homogeneity fails. Problem 2: discontinuous and not convex; the source says minimizing it is NP-hard.

steps.label: KP09 · 1/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: With many features one basically tries every combination of which coordinates are non-zero.

steps.label: KP09 · 2/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Figure: red is ℓ0, 0 only at 0 and 1 elsewhere; the green V of |x| is the nearest convex function on [−1, 1]. Analogy: ℓ0 is a flat monthly fee for using it at all, ℓ1 charges by amount used.) The fix is to replace it with its nearest convex function, a convex relaxation: the ℓ1 norm.

steps.label: KP09 · 2/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Figure: red is ℓ0, 0 only at 0 and 1 elsewhere; the green V of |x| is the nearest convex function on [−1, 1]. Analogy: ℓ0 is a flat monthly fee for using it at all, ℓ1 charges by amount used.) The fix is to replace it with its nearest convex function, a convex relaxation: the ℓ1 norm.

steps.label: KP09 · 2/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: This gives lasso: minimize J(x;θ) + α‖x‖₁, the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator.

steps.label: KP09 · 2/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: ℓ1 is convex, so when J is convex the whole objective is convex and reliable algorithms exist.

steps.label: KP09 · 3/14
steps.speakerNotes: Blue is x²: smooth and flat at 0, so ℓ2 only shrinks.

steps.label: KP09 · 3/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Blue is x²: smooth and flat at 0, so ℓ2 only shrinks.

steps.label: KP09 · 3/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Green is |x|: a corner at x = 0, non-differentiable; that corner is why it can produce exact zeros.

steps.label: KP09 · 3/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The price is non-differentiability, handled with the subgradient; the next section works out the soft threshold.

steps.label: KP09 · 4/14
steps.speakerNotes: Continuing: the simplest case, one coordinate, J's quadratic approximation ½h(x − x*)² with h > 0, plus the ℓ1 penalty.

steps.label: KP09 · 4/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Continuing: the simplest case, one coordinate, J's quadratic approximation ½h(x − x*)² with h > 0, plus the ℓ1 penalty.

steps.label: KP09 · 4/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The blue parabola fits the data, the green |x| keeps it simple and has the corner. (Illustration; x* taken as 1.5.)

steps.label: KP09 · 4/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The minimum satisfies 0 ∈ subgradient: h(x − x*) + αs = 0 with s in the subdifferential of |x|. Three cases next.

steps.label: KP09 · 5/14
steps.speakerNotes: (The three plots are the actual curves of ½h(x − x*)² + α|x| for h = 2, α = 1; the minima 0.7, −0.3, 0 are verified in code.) x > 0: s = 1, so x = x* − α/h; consistent with x > 0 only if x* > α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 5/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (The three plots are the actual curves of ½h(x − x*)² + α|x| for h = 2, α = 1; the minima 0.7, −0.3, 0 are verified in code.) x > 0: s = 1, so x = x* − α/h; consistent with x > 0 only if x* > α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 5/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: x < 0: s = −1, so x = x* + α/h; consistent with x < 0 only if x* < −α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 5/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: x = 0: s may be any number in [−1, 1]; −hx* + αs = 0 has a solution iff |hx*| ≤ α, i.e. |x*| ≤ α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 6/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Top row six x*: −2, −0.8, −0.3, 0.3, 1.2, 2; bottom row the matching x†: −1.5, −0.3, 0, 0, 0.7, 1.5; green arrows mean absorbed to 0 by the dead zone.) Together the three cases are the soft threshold: subtract α/h when x* > α/h; 0 when |x*| ≤ α/h; add α/h when x* < −α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 6/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Top row six x*: −2, −0.8, −0.3, 0.3, 1.2, 2; bottom row the matching x†: −1.5, −0.3, 0, 0, 0.7, 1.5; green arrows mean absorbed to 0 by the dead zone.) Together the three cases are the soft threshold: subtract α/h when x* > α/h; 0 when |x*| ≤ α/h; add α/h when x* < −α/h.

steps.label: KP09 · 6/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: As one line: x† = sign(x*) · max(|x*| − α/h, 0).

steps.label: KP09 · 6/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: In plain words: coefficients within the threshold α/h are switched off to zero; those beyond it are translated toward zero by α/h, direction unchanged.

steps.label: KP09 · 7/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Each row is a number line: white dot x*, orange dot the ℓ1 soft-threshold result, blue dot the ℓ2 result, gold band the dead zone.) h = 2, α = 1, threshold α/h = 0.5. x* = 1.2: above 0.5, subtract 0.5 to get 0.7; ℓ2 gives 0.8.

steps.label: KP09 · 7/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Each row is a number line: white dot x*, orange dot the ℓ1 soft-threshold result, blue dot the ℓ2 result, gold band the dead zone.) h = 2, α = 1, threshold α/h = 0.5. x* = 1.2: above 0.5, subtract 0.5 to get 0.7; ℓ2 gives 0.8.

steps.label: KP09 · 7/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: x* = 0.3: within 0.5, switched off to 0; ℓ2 gives 0.2.

steps.label: KP09 · 7/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: x* = −0.8: below −0.5, add 0.5 to get −0.3; ℓ2 gives −0.5333. All three were checked on a fine grid.

steps.label: KP09 · 8/14
steps.speakerNotes: The dashed line is the no-shrink diagonal; blue is ℓ2, a line of slope below 1 with no dead zone.

steps.label: KP09 · 8/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The dashed line is the no-shrink diagonal; blue is ℓ2, a line of slope below 1 with no dead zone.

steps.label: KP09 · 8/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Orange is the soft threshold: flat zero between −0.5 and 0.5, ℓ1's dead zone; outside it parallel to the diagonal, a fixed 0.5 lower.

steps.label: KP09 · 8/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The three green dots are the last page's three rows. ℓ2 shrinks large coefficients proportionally more; ℓ1 subtracts the same α/h from every coefficient outside the threshold.

steps.label: KP09 · 9/14
steps.speakerNotes: With many coordinates, minimizing J + α‖x‖₁ can be replaced by the equivalent constrained form: minimize J within ‖x‖₁ ≤ r; the larger α, the smaller r. (Added)

steps.label: KP09 · 9/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: With many coordinates, minimizing J + α‖x‖₁ can be replaced by the equivalent constrained form: minimize J within ‖x‖₁ ≤ r; the larger α, the smaller r. (Added)

steps.label: KP09 · 9/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: With two coordinates the ℓ1 region is a diamond and the ℓ2 region a circle.

steps.label: KP09 · 9/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: J's contours are ellipses; the minimum is where an ellipse growing from x* first touches the region.

steps.label: KP09 · 10/14
steps.speakerNotes: Take x* = (1.6, 0.9), H = [[2, 1.2], [1.2, 1.5]], r = 1. Blue ellipses are J's contours; the orange one just touches the region, the orange dot is the contact point. (Found by scanning the boundary.)

steps.label: KP09 · 10/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Take x* = (1.6, 0.9), H = [[2, 1.2], [1.2, 1.5]], r = 1. Blue ellipses are J's contours; the orange one just touches the region, the orange dot is the contact point. (Found by scanning the boundary.)

steps.label: KP09 · 10/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Left: the circle is smooth, the contact (0.81, 0.59) lies mid-arc, neither coordinate is zero, J = 0.9951.

steps.label: KP09 · 10/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Right: the diamond has corners; the contour hits a corner first, contact at the vertex (1.00, 0.00), J = 1.6155, the second coordinate exactly zero.

steps.label: KP09 · 11/14
steps.speakerNotes: Same x*, H replaced by another positive-definite matrix [[1.5, −0.9], [−0.9, 1]]; the ellipse changes shape and direction.

steps.label: KP09 · 11/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Same x*, H replaced by another positive-definite matrix [[1.5, −0.9], [−0.9, 1]]; the ellipse changes shape and direction.

steps.label: KP09 · 11/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The minimum on the diamond becomes (0.9372, 0.0628), not on an axis. (Found by scanning the boundary.)

steps.label: KP09 · 11/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Eigenvalues go from about 0.52, 2.98 to 0.32, 2.18. So the corner makes exact zeros easy, not certain.

steps.label: KP09 · 12/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Two 10 × 10 grids, each square = 1%: ℓ1 fills 63 (62.6%), ℓ2 fills none, with only a sliver in the first square for 0.1%.) Now statistics over 2819 random x* and positive-definite H (fixed seed, with ‖x*‖₁ > 1).

steps.label: KP09 · 12/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Two 10 × 10 grids, each square = 1%: ℓ1 fills 63 (62.6%), ℓ2 fills none, with only a sliver in the first square for 0.1%.) Now statistics over 2819 random x* and positive-definite H (fixed seed, with ‖x*‖₁ > 1).

steps.label: KP09 · 12/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The ℓ1 minimum lands on an axis in 62.6% of cases; ℓ2 only 0.1% (a grid-resolution boundary artefact, theoretically probability 0). (Lecture numbers, not re-run.)

steps.label: KP09 · 12/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: So the right statement: the ℓ1 corner makes exact zeros very common; ℓ2 almost never.

steps.label: KP09 · 13/14
steps.speakerNotes: (Left: contours for H = [[2, 1.2], [1.2, 1.5]], x* = (1.6, 0.9), with the coordinate-wise point and the true lasso solution; right: the ℓ1 diamond and ℓ2 circle of radius 3: v = (3, 0) sits on a diamond corner, after a 30° turn it stays on the circle but leaves the diamond.) Premise: the last derivation assumed a diagonal Hessian, coordinates independent. A general H is not diagonal, and thresholding each coordinate once is then not the right answer.

steps.label: KP09 · 13/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: (Left: contours for H = [[2, 1.2], [1.2, 1.5]], x* = (1.6, 0.9), with the coordinate-wise point and the true lasso solution; right: the ℓ1 diamond and ℓ2 circle of radius 3: v = (3, 0) sits on a diamond corner, after a 30° turn it stays on the circle but leaves the diamond.) Premise: the last derivation assumed a diagonal Hessian, coordinates independent. A general H is not diagonal, and thresholding each coordinate once is then not the right answer.

steps.label: KP09 · 13/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The example (α = 1): coordinate-wise soft threshold with thresholds α/h_jj = 0.5, 0.667 gives (1.1, 0.2333), objective 2.3167; the true lasso solution is (1.4077, 0.3872), objective 2.1474, lower.

steps.label: KP09 · 13/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Nor can we rotate to eigen-directions as in KP08: ℓ2 is unchanged by rotation, ℓ1 is not (v = (3, 0) has ℓ1 = 3, after 30° it is 4.0981); the diamond's corners are tied to the axes. Added: in practice coordinate descent repeats coordinate updates until stable.

steps.label: KP09 · 14/14
steps.speakerNotes: The larger α, the more zeros, but larger is not always better: too large switches off truly useful features.

steps.label: KP09 · 14/14 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The larger α, the more zeros, but larger is not always better: too large switches off truly useful features.

steps.label: KP09 · 14/14 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Choose α as KP07 said, by a validation set or cross-validation.

steps.label: KP09 · 14/14 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Next: ℓ2 and ℓ1 both add a term to the objective. Can we leave the objective alone and only train fewer steps? That is KP10: early stopping.
